page.title: Scanning
page.info: Every way the box finds devices, identifies them and checks them for vulnerabilities, with the memory each takes and when it runs. The scope, window, speed, exclusions and fragile types are set once, under Safety, for every engine on your LAN.
page.infoContext: To scan now: Scan the LAN now on the Network discovery card or the Devices list, Scan selected on the Devices list, Check this device now on a device, Deep scan now on a public target.

discover.title: Discover
discover.description: Find which devices are on your network.
discover.info: Passive listening hears devices that talk; network discovery asks each address of your LAN ranges, gently, inside the time window.

identify.title: Identify
identify.description: Learn what each device is: maker, model, software and versions.
identify.info: Versions are what Vedette matches with the list of vulnerabilities exploited in the wild, so the better a device is identified, the fewer vulnerabilities are missed or wrongly reported.

vuln.title: Check vulnerabilities
vuln.description: Confirm known vulnerabilities with safe checks.
vuln.info: Checks only read or confirm; none is meant to change anything. On your LAN they follow the shared safety settings. Scans of your public IPs and domains follow each target's own testing terms instead.

traps.title: Traps
traps.description: Decoys that raise an alert when anyone touches them.
traps.info: A decoy has no real use, so any touch is suspicious. Traps send nothing to your devices.

passive.name: Passive listening
passive.finds: Devices that talk on your network, without sending anything to them.
passive.where: Sensor and its card: Devices, Sensor and agents, Sensor

nmap-discovery.name: Network discovery (nmap)
nmap-discovery.finds: Devices that answer on your LAN ranges.

nmap-versions.name: Service versions (nmap)

nmap-versions.where: Which device types get them: Safety, Fragile devices

snmp.finds: Model, firmware and serial number of switches, printers and UPS.

openvas.finds: Thousands of network vulnerability checks on your public IPs.

honeypot.name: Decoys (honeypot)

honeypot.where: Trap IPs: Internal traps, Trap IPs

adminOnly: Only an administrator can turn engines on or off.

box.memory: Engines that are on: up to {{used}} of this box's {{total}} of memory.
box.memoryInfo: Upper limits, Vedette's core included: the engines use less most of the time.
box.overTitle: The engines' memory limits add up to more than this box has
box.over: If Vedette's core and every engine that is on reached their limits at the same time, they would need {{used}}; this box has {{total}}. The limits are upper bounds, not what they use all the time, so this is fine while the box stays responsive. If the box slows down or a scan stops for lack of memory, turn off an engine you do not need.
box.overViewer: If Vedette's core and every engine that is on reached their limits at the same time, they would need {{used}}; this box has {{total}}. The limits are upper bounds, not what they use all the time, so this is fine while the box stays responsive. If the box slows down, an administrator can turn off an engine that is not needed.
box.biggest: {{name}} holds the most while it is on: up to {{size}}.

cost.none: none of its own (runs inside the box's core)

scope.dialogDescription: Vedette scans nothing outside these ranges.
scope.dialogInfo: Internal IPv4 ranges only (RFC 1918 or 100.64.0.0/10). They stay editable under Settings, Scanning, Safety.
scope.changed: The ranges changed since this dialog opened (another admin or tab). The current list is shown: check it and tick again.

module.depsTitle: Turn on {{name}} and what it needs?

safety.adminOnly: Only an administrator can change these settings. You can still read them.
safety.appliesTo: Set once for every engine on your LAN: network discovery, service versions, SNMP and the vulnerability checks. Scans of your public targets follow their own testing terms and are not covered here yet, except the window: their scheduled scans start only inside it.
safety.scopeDescription: Your LAN ranges and your confirmation that you may scan them.
safety.scopeInfo: Nothing outside these ranges is ever scanned. Changing the ranges asks for the confirmation again.
safety.confirmAgain: The ranges changed: tick the confirmation again to save.
safety.notConfirmed: Not confirmed yet: nothing on the LAN is scanned until you tick it.
safety.windowDescription: Discovery, version scans, SNMP rounds and scheduled checks run only inside it.
safety.windowInfo: Read in the organization time zone ({{zone}}). A window that crosses midnight (22:00 to 05:00) counts by its start day. Scan now is not bound by it; the scheduled scans of your public targets start only inside it.
safety.speedDescription: Lower is gentler on old devices.
safety.ppsHint: nmap and SNMP, in packets per second.
safety.exclDescription: Addresses no engine touches on your LAN.
safety.exclInfo: The Vedette box needs no line here: it is never part of a sweep.
safety.fragileDescription: Scanned once, gently, when first seen; listened to only after that.
safety.fragileInfo: Every type acting as one of these counts. "Allow regular scans" keeps that type in the regular scans.
safety.fragileDevices_one: {{count}} fragile device today: see it on Devices
safety.fragileDevices_other: {{count}} fragile devices today: see them on Devices
safety.changedElsewhere: Someone else saved these settings after you opened this page, so nothing was saved yet.

merge.taken: {{part}}: changed by them, now {{value}}. Shown below.
merge.bothChanged: {{part}}: you both changed it. Your edit is kept below; theirs is {{value}}.
merge.saveAgain: Everything you typed is still in the form. Check it, then save again.

cost.line: One pass: {{addresses}} addresses, at least {{pass}} at {{pps}} packets/s
cost.nights: It needs {{windows}} scan windows of {{window}}: the sweep is one run that goes on each night where it stopped. To finish in one window, raise the scan rate, widen the window or narrow the ranges.
cost.tooLarge: It needs {{windows}} scan windows of {{window}}, and a week has {{week}}. Saving is refused: raise the scan rate, widen the window or add days, or narrow the ranges.

saveBlocked.bad_one: Fix or remove the range marked in red to save.
saveBlocked.bad_other: Fix or remove the {{count}} ranges marked in red to save.
saveBlocked.tooLarge: Saving is refused: one pass of this scope does not fit a week of scan windows.

range.title: Network ranges
range.refused: The scope with this range would be refused on save: change the scan rate, the window or the ranges first.
range.label: Network range
range.hint: With its prefix length, for example 192.168.10.0/24.
range.hintInfo: Internal addresses only: 10.x, 172.16 to 172.31, 192.168.x, 100.64 to 100.127. Other prefix lengths work too, for example 192.168.10.0/25. At most 16 ranges.
range.none: No range yet. Add at least one range to let Vedette scan.
range.note: {{from}} was added as {{to}}, the first address of its range.

problem.empty: Type a range first. Write it like 192.168.10.0/24.
problem.noPrefix: "{{value}}" has no prefix length. Add it so Vedette scans the right size of network, for example {{value}}/24 or {{value}}/25.
problem.format: "{{value}}" is not a valid range. Write it like 192.168.10.0/24.
problem.hostBits: {{value}} is not written correctly: the address part must be the first address of the range. Use {{net}}.
problem.notPrivate: {{value}} is not an internal range, so it cannot be added here. To scan public addresses, use External exposure after verifying ownership.
problem.overlap: {{value}} overlaps {{other}}, which is already in the list. Keep the larger range and remove the smaller one.

excl.label: IP address or network
excl.bad: Enter one IP (192.168.10.10) or a network (192.168.10.0/28, where the address part is the first address of the range).

scanNow.queuedToast: Queued: it starts when the scanner is free
scanNow.sweepRunning: A LAN scan is going on now.
scanNow.needsScope: The network ranges are not confirmed yet.

nmap.out_of_scope_other: {{count}} outside the network ranges or excluded

device.box: The Vedette box itself is never part of a network scan.
device.no_ip: No IP address yet, so network discovery cannot check it. Add its IP on this page.

both.no_ip: No IP address yet, so Vedette can neither identify this device nor run vulnerability checks on it. Add its IP on this page.

device.manual: Added by hand: network discovery checks it only once you turn its network scan on under Sources on its device page.
device.manualServices: Its network scan is off: Sources, on the Overview tab, turns it on.
device.never: Set to never scan, or its network scan is off under Sources: network discovery does not check it.
device.out_of_scope: Outside the network ranges or excluded: network discovery does not check it. Settings, Scanning, Safety holds the ranges.
device.scope: The network ranges are not confirmed yet, so network discovery checks no device. Settings, Scanning, Safety confirms them.
device.discovery_off: Network discovery is off, so it checks no device. Settings, Scanning, Engines turns it on.

hint.vulnNone_one: No suspected finding on this device has a safe check: none exists for its suspected CVE, so a run would confirm nothing. Its installed version, read by SNMP or an agent, decides it, or use Confirm on the finding.
hint.vulnNone_other: No suspected finding on this device has a safe check: none exists for these {{count}} suspected CVEs, so a run would confirm nothing. The installed version, read by SNMP or an agent, decides them, or use Confirm on each finding.
hint.vulnNoneSuspected: No suspected finding on this device has a safe check: nothing on it is suspected, and no confirmed finding has a check to run again, so a run would do nothing.
hint.vulnCount: {{checkable}} of {{count}} suspected findings can be checked.
hint.vulnAgain_one: {{count}} confirmed finding can be checked again, to see whether a fix holds.
hint.vulnAgain_other: {{count}} confirmed findings can be checked again, to see whether a fix holds.
hint.identify: Finds its open ports, services, operating system and software versions. Does not test whether a flaw can be exploited. Usually 1 to 5 minutes.
hint.vuln: Tries Vedette’s checks for the exploited flaws this device may have, to confirm or rule them out. Identifies it first; patches nothing. Usually 5 to 15 minutes.

lastChecks.title: Last checks

kind.vuln: Vulnerability check: does a known exploit work

lastChecks.neverIdentify: “Check this device now” above runs it. Network discovery also checks each new device, and every device weekly, in the scan window.
lastChecks.neverIdentifyRole: An admin can run it with “Check this device now” above. Network discovery also checks each new device, and every device weekly, in the scan window.
lastChecks.neverVuln: “Run vulnerability checks now” above runs it. A newly exploited flaw that matches this device can start one too.
lastChecks.neverVulnRole: An operator can run it with “Run vulnerability checks now” above. A newly exploited flaw that matches this device can start one too.

vulnWhy.no_ip: No IP address yet, so no vulnerability check can run on it. Add its IP on this page.
vulnWhy.regular_scan_never: Set to never scan, or its network scan is off under Sources: no vulnerability check runs on it.
vulnWhy.unapproved: Not approved yet: vulnerability checks run on it only once you approve it on this page.
vulnWhy.excluded: In the exclusion list: no vulnerability check runs on it. Settings, Scanning, Safety holds the list.
vulnWhy.out_of_scope: Outside the confirmed network ranges: no vulnerability check runs on it. Settings, Scanning, Safety holds the ranges.

lastChecks.vulnOff: The vulnerability checks (Preview) are off, so none runs.
lastChecks.vulnOffLink: Turn them on: Settings, Scanning, Engines
lastChecks.neverSnmp: An SNMP read runs in the scan window once SNMP is set up on this device.
lastChecks.notReadYetInfo: SNMP is set up on this device. The next scan window reads it, or press Check now on its SNMP row.
